# opencode-img_prompt

An [opencode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that renders your typed prompt as an
image and sends **the image** to the model instead of the text. For dense
prompts this can dramatically cut *fresh input tokens*, because a screenshot is
billed at a fixed vision-tile cost regardless of how much text it contains.

You type a prompt, hit enter, and the plugin transparently swaps your text for a
PNG of that text before the message reaches the model.

---

## Why?

Text tokens scale linearly with the length of your prompt. A rendered image of
that same text bills at a roughly **fixed** vision cost. So the denser the
prompt, the bigger the potential savings.

### Findings

Measured with `prompt-ab-test.nu` against a live opencode server
(`gitlab/duo-chat-haiku-4-5`), sending the identical prompt twice — once as an
image, once as text. "Fresh input tokens" is the `input` field of the assistant
message (excludes shared cached system/tool overhead, which is identical for
both variants and only dilutes the comparison).

| Prompt                     | Approx. size | Text fresh input tokens | Image fresh input tokens | Reduction |
| -------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------- | ------------------------ | --------- |
| One-line prompt            | ~10 chars    | 326                     | 327                      | none (image is *worse*) |
| 7 paragraphs "lorem ipsum" | ~4.6 KB      | 1722                    | 330                      | ~81%      |
| 60 dense lines             | ~8.3 KB      | 2362                    | 330                      | ~86%      |

Key takeaways:

- The image's fresh input cost stays **flat (~327 tokens)** no matter how much
  text you pack into it — that is the fixed vision-tile floor.
- The text variant grows linearly with prompt length.
- Your exact numbers will vary by model, provider tokenizer, and image
  dimensions.

### Finding the crossover (recommended `minChars`)

To pick a sensible `minChars`, prompts of increasing length were sent as both
text and image (same model as above). Because the image floor is fixed, there is
a break-even length below which the text is actually cheaper:

| Prompt length | Text tokens | Image tokens | Tokens saved | % saved |
| ------------- | ----------- | ------------ | ------------ | ------- |
| 10 chars      | 326         | 327          | -1           | worse   |
| 25 chars      | 328         | 327          | 1            | ~0%     |
| 100 chars     | 348         | 327          | 21           | 6%      |
| 200 chars     | 378         | 327          | 51           | 13.5%   |
| 300 chars     | 402         | 327          | 75           | 18.7%   |
| 400 chars     | 431         | 327          | 104          | 24.1%   |
| 600 chars     | 487         | 327          | 160          | 32.9%   |
| 900 chars     | 570         | 327          | 243          | 42.6%   |
| 1500 chars    | 732         | 327          | 405          | 55.3%   |

The raw break-even is only ~20 characters, but savings that close to the
crossover are a handful of tokens — not worth accepting any OCR risk for. Savings
become **meaningful (>10%) at roughly 200 characters** and climb steeply from
there.

**Recommended: `minChars = 200`.** Below that, prompts stay as plain text (no
risk, negligible cost); at or above it, they convert to an image for real
savings. Lower it toward `0` if you want to maximize token savings and trust
your model's OCR; raise it if you want to reserve the feature for only large
prompts.

> These figures are a snapshot from one model. Per-model benchmarking is planned
> (see [Roadmap](#roadmap)); until then, treat the numbers as directional and the
> `minChars` recommendation as a safe default rather than a tuned optimum.

---

## ⚠️ Important warnings

- **Not all models support image input (vision).** Models without vision will
  error, ignore the image, or behave unpredictably. Only enable this plugin when
  your target model accepts image input.
- **OCR accuracy varies by model.** Even among vision-capable models, how
  reliably the model reads text from an image differs a lot. Some models read a
  dense screenshot flawlessly; others misread characters, skip lines, or — as
  observed in testing — treat the inline image as a *file to go find on disk*
  rather than content to read. If responses seem to ignore your prompt, your
  model's OCR is likely the culprit.
- **This is a token/quality tradeoff.** You are trading guaranteed-lossless text
  for cheaper-but-lossy OCR. For correctness-critical prompts, verify your model
  handles it before relying on it.

---

## Requirements

- **opencode** with plugin support (`@opencode-ai/plugin` >= 1.1.0).
- **ImageMagick 7** (`magick` on your `PATH`). Install via `brew install
  imagemagick` (macOS) or your platform's package manager.
- A **vision-capable model** as your active model.

The rendering font ([JetBrains Mono](https://www.jetbrains.com/lp/mono/), SIL
OFL 1.1) is **bundled with the plugin**, so no system font is required and
behavior is identical across macOS, Linux, and Windows. You can still override
it (see [Configuration](#configuration)).

---

## Installation

### Preferred — `opencode plugin` command

The `opencode plugin` subcommand installs the plugin and updates your
`opencode.json` automatically, including seeding the recommended
`{ "minChars": 200 }` default. This is the least error-prone path.

```bash
# provide the --global flag (or run outside of a project) to install to your global configuration
opencode plugin opencode-img-prompt
# or from a local checkout of this repo (by path)
opencode plugin /path/to/opencode-img_prompt
```

This will add an entry to the `plugin` array in the relevant `opencode.json` file:

```json
{
  "plugin": [["opencode-img-prompt", { "minChars": 200 }]]
}
```

You can edit those options afterward — see [Configuration](#configuration).

### Manual — copy into the plugin directory

If you'd rather install by hand, copy the plugin into your opencode plugin directory.
`opencode` auto-loads any `*.ts` / `*.js` placed **directly** under these folders:

- Project: `.opencode/plugin/`
- Global: `~/.config/opencode/plugin/`

opencode does not scan nested subfolders, so copy the **contents** of this repo's
`plugin/` directory (keeping `img-prompt.ts` at the top level). The bundled font
must sit in a `fonts/` folder next to `img-prompt.ts`, since the plugin resolves
it relative to its own location. The resulting layout:

```
~/.config/opencode/
├── opencode.json                     # your existing config (optional)
└── plugin/
    ├── img-prompt.ts                 # the plugin entry point (must be here, not nested)
    └── fonts/
        ├── JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf
        └── OFL.txt
```

```bash
# global install — copy the plugin CONTENTS (keeps img-prompt.ts at the top level)
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugin
cp -R plugin/. ~/.config/opencode/plugin/
```

For a **project-local** install instead, use `.opencode/plugin/` at your repo
root with the same flat structure:

```
<your-project>/
├── opencode.json
└── .opencode/
    └── plugin/
        ├── img-prompt.ts
        └── fonts/
            ├── JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf
            └── OFL.txt
```

> If you have multiple local plugins, they all share the `plugin/` directory.
> Just keep each plugin's `.ts` file at the top level; the `fonts/` folder is
> only used by this plugin.

With a manual install you configure options yourself — either via the tuple form
in `opencode.json` or via environment variables (see
[Configuration](#configuration)). To pass options to a manually installed local
file, reference it by path in the `plugin` array:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": [
    ["~/.config/opencode/plugin/img-prompt.ts", { "minChars": 200 }]
  ]
}
```

After any install method, **quit and restart opencode** — plugins load once at
startup.

---

## Usage

Just type a prompt and hit enter. The plugin intercepts the message, renders
your text to a PNG, and replaces the text with the image (plus a short companion
instruction telling the model to read the image).

That's it — no command, no flag. To confirm it's active, a converted message
shows a `prompt.png` attachment instead of your raw text.

To disable it, set `enabled: false` in your `opencode.json` plugin options, or
set `IMG_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` in your environment before launching opencode.

---

## Configuration

The plugin can be configured two ways. Options are resolved with this precedence
(highest first):

1. **`opencode.json` plugin options** — the recommended, per-project method.
2. **Environment variables** (`IMG_PROMPT_*`) — a fallback, handy for the
   zero-config auto-load install or temporary overrides.
3. Built-in defaults.

### Via `opencode.json` (recommended)

Use the tuple form in the `plugin` array — `[name, options]` — exactly like
other opencode plugins. Reference the plugin by its npm name (if installed from
npm) or by file path (for a local install):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": [
    [
      "opencode-img-prompt",
      {
        "minChars": 200,
        "width": 900,
        "fontSize": 24,
        "background": "#1e1e2e",
        "foreground": "#cdd6f4"
      }
    ]
  ]
}
```

Local-file form (adjust the path to wherever you installed it):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": [
    ["~/.config/opencode/plugin/img-prompt.ts", { "minChars": 200 }]
  ]
}
```

> When you use the config-tuple form with a file path, reference the file
> directly and it is loaded with your options. (Files auto-discovered from
> `plugin/` load with defaults only — so to pass options to a local install,
> either point the tuple at the file or use env vars.)

### Options

| `opencode.json` key | Env var                 | Default               | Description                                                        |
| ------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `enabled`           | `IMG_PROMPT_DISABLED`   | `true`                | Set `enabled: false` (or any truthy `IMG_PROMPT_DISABLED`) to disable. |
| `fontSize`          | `IMG_PROMPT_FONT_SIZE`  | `24`                  | Font size in points.                                               |
| `width`             | `IMG_PROMPT_WIDTH`      | `900`                 | Wrap width in pixels.                                              |
| `padding`           | `IMG_PROMPT_PADDING`    | `40`                  | Padding around the text in pixels.                                 |
| `background`        | `IMG_PROMPT_BACKGROUND` | `#1e1e2e`             | Background color (any ImageMagick color spec).                     |
| `foreground`        | `IMG_PROMPT_FOREGROUND` | `#cdd6f4`             | Text color.                                                        |
| `font`              | `IMG_PROMPT_FONT`       | bundled JetBrains Mono| Path to a font file passed to ImageMagick `-font`.                 |
| `minChars`          | `IMG_PROMPT_MIN_CHARS`  | `0`                   | Only convert prompts at least this many characters. `0` = always. |
| `instruction`       | `IMG_PROMPT_INSTRUCTION`| see source            | Companion text sent with the image. Set to empty to omit.         |

**Recommended: set `minChars` to `200`** (see
[Finding the crossover](#finding-the-crossover-recommended-minchars)). Below ~200
characters the token savings are negligible and not worth any OCR risk; at or
above it the image starts saving 13%+ and rising.

The bundled JetBrains Mono font is used by default and works on every OS. Only
set `font` if you want a different typeface.

---

## Included tools

Two standalone Nushell scripts are bundled (used to produce the findings above):

- **`prompt-screenshot.nu`** — render a prompt to a PNG. Copies to the macOS
  clipboard by default; pass `-o file.png` to write to disk instead.

  ```bash
  ./prompt-screenshot.nu "some prompt text"
  echo "some prompt text" | ./prompt-screenshot.nu -o out.png
  ```

- **`prompt-ab-test.nu`** — send the same prompt to a running opencode server as
  both image and text, and print a token/cost comparison.

  ```bash
  opencode serve --port 4096         # in another terminal
  cat AGENTS.md | ./prompt-ab-test.nu \
    --server http://127.0.0.1:4096 \
    --model gitlab/duo-chat-haiku-4-5
  ```

Both require [Nushell](https://www.nushell.sh/) and ImageMagick.

---

## How it works

The plugin hooks opencode's `chat.message` event, which fires when a user
message is received and exposes its `parts` array. The plugin:

1. Collects the user-authored text parts (skipping synthetic/injected ones).
2. Renders the combined text to a PNG with ImageMagick's auto-wrapping
   `caption:` operator, emitted to stdout as `png:-`.
3. Base64-encodes it into a `data:image/png;base64,...` URL.
4. Replaces the text part(s) with a single `file` part (the image) and prepends
   a small synthetic instruction text part.

If rendering fails for any reason, the original text is left untouched so your
prompt still reaches the model.

---

## Roadmap

- Per-model OCR accuracy benchmarking and a compatibility matrix.
- Automatic fallback to text when the active model lacks vision.
- Optional side-by-side (image + text) mode for correctness-sensitive prompts.
